q: The data processing inequality states that for a Markov chain X → Y → Z:
opts: I(X;Z) ≤ I(X;Y) (processing data cannot increase mutual information)
exp: Data processing inequality: if X → Y → Z is Markov, then I(X;Z) ≤ I(X;Y). Processing (applying a channel to Y) cannot increase the information about X. This fundamental inequality underpins the channel coding theorem and source-channel separation.
